Final independent closure check: Reduced acyclicity gives ker d_j = closure ran d_(j-1). If L_j x=0, its quadratic form yields d_j x=0 and d_(j-1)^* x=0. Thus x lies in that closed range and is orthogonal to it, hence x=0. The endpoint and zero-space cases are included.

Final independent closure check: If L_j G_j=I, then L_j(G_j L_j-I)=0. Injectivity gives G_j L_j=I. A bounded right inverse therefore is exactly a bounded two-sided inverse under the existing assumptions.

Final independent closure check: For the length-one complex on complex l2 with d=diag(1/n), injectivity and dense range give both reduced records zero. A bounded contraction would send e_n to n e_n. A right inverse of L=diag(1/n^2) would send e_n to n^2 e_n. Both are impossible.

Final independent closure check: The reference's conditional closed-range proof retains ||G_j|| <= M_j^2 and finite maxima of the operator norms. It does not infer existence or a positive lower bound merely from reduced acyclicity.

Final independent closure check: Any complete counterexample to the requested universal conjunction suffices. The rubric remains unchanged and does not require the author example, closed-range classification, or displayed contraction formula.
